title: Account Opening Document Verification
summary: Check OVDs, PAN, masked Aadhaar, photographs and entity documents in an account opening file against each other and against CKYC, with mismatches routed to an officer.

seo.title: Account Opening Document Verification with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that checks KYC documents for savings and current account opening, cross-matches names, addresses and photos, and flags mismatches for officers.

problem.intro: A savings account file is a few pages, but a current account for a partnership or private limited company can run to dozens: KYC of every partner or director, beneficial-owner declarations, board resolutions and registration certificates. Central processing teams re-check what branch staff already looked at, and discrepancies surface only after the customer has left the branch.

pain_points.title: Name and address mismatches across documents
pain_points.detail: Initials, spelling variants and transliterated names differ between PAN, OVD and the application form, and officers decide each case by eye with no record of why.

pain_points.title: Entity documents checked inconsistently
pain_points.detail: Partnership deeds, MOA and AOA, board resolutions and beneficial-ownership declarations are long, and the authorised signatory clause is easy to misread.

pain_points.title: Rework between branch and central processing
pain_points.detail: Files bounce back for a missing self-attestation, an expired passport or an unsigned FATCA declaration, delaying account activation.

pain_points.title: Weak signals of tampering
pain_points.detail: Edited PAN images, swapped photographs and documents reused across applications are hard to spot when each file is reviewed on its own.

solution.overview: We build a verification layer that sits between your onboarding channel and account activation. It splits each file into documents, identifies the type of every page and extracts the fields your KYC checklist needs. It then cross-checks name, date of birth, address and photograph across documents, compares them with the CKYC record and PAN verification response where your bank has access, and applies your checklist for individuals, proprietorships, partnerships, LLPs, companies and trusts. Each check returns pass, fail or needs review, with the source page highlighted. Central processing officers work a ranked queue and confirm or override every flag.
capabilities: Classifies OVDs, PAN, masked Aadhaar, photographs, FATCA/CRS forms and entity documents page by page
Fuzzy name matching that handles initials, transliteration and Hindi or regional-script names
Photograph comparison between the OVD and the live or branch-captured photo, sent for review on low similarity
Product checklists for proprietorship, partnership, LLP, company and trust accounts, including beneficial-owner details
Tamper indicators on images and PDFs, plus reuse detection across recent applications
Reads authorised-signatory and operating-mandate clauses from board resolutions and deeds

workflow.title: Receive the onboarding file
workflow.detail: Documents arrive from the branch scanner, tab-based onboarding app or digital journey, grouped under the application reference.

workflow.title: Classify and extract
workflow.detail: Each page is typed and the fields for that document type are extracted, with Aadhaar numbers masked at intake.

workflow.title: Cross-check and look up
workflow.detail: Names, dates, addresses and photographs are compared across documents and against CKYC and PAN verification responses.

workflow.title: Apply the product checklist
workflow.detail: Rules for the customer type and account variant confirm that every mandatory document, signature and declaration is present and valid.

workflow.title: Officer review
workflow.detail: Mismatches, missing items and tamper signals go to a central processing officer, who confirms, overrides or requests documents.

workflow.title: Hand over to account opening
workflow.detail: Verified data, the checklist result and the evidence trail are posted to the account opening module or a CBS staging layer.

inputs: Account opening form and KYC declarations
OVDs such as passport, driving licence, voter ID or masked Aadhaar
Customer photograph and specimen signature card
Entity documents: partnership deed, MOA and AOA, board resolution, registration certificates
outputs: Structured KYC record per applicant and related person
Checklist result with pass, fail or review per item
Mismatch and tamper flags with source-page links
Audit trail ready for internal and concurrent audit
human_in_the_loop: Central processing officers review every flagged mismatch, missing document and tamper signal, and they alone mark a file as KYC-complete. Photograph similarity is a prompt for review, never an automatic rejection.
integrations: Core banking system or account opening module (via API or staging table)
CKYC registry access through the bank's existing CERSAI integration
PAN verification service already used by the bank
Tab banking or digital onboarding app
guardrails: Aadhaar masked at intake so only the last four digits remain, per UIDAI rules
No auto-rejection: low-similarity photos and mismatches always go to an officer
Thresholds per check agreed with compliance and reviewed regularly
Personal data masked in logs and processed in the bank's chosen region
Sampling of auto-passed files for quality assurance
compliance_notes: Designed to support customer due diligence under the RBI KYC Master Direction; KYC sign-off stays with the bank.
Supports data minimisation and purpose limitation under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: Current account opening for proprietorship and partnership firms at one central processing unit, run on de-identified historical files and then on a live shadow sample.
deliverables: Checklist and extraction schema agreed with operations and compliance
Working verification pipeline on de-identified files
Accuracy and flag-quality report against officer decisions
Production plan with integration approach and cost

what_we_measure.metric: Field extraction accuracy by document type
what_we_measure.how: Compared with values keyed by central processing officers for the same files.
Raised flags that officers confirm as genuine discrepancies, by flag type.
Discrepancies officers found that the system did not flag, logged during parallel review.
Timed on a sample of files reviewed with and without the system.

faqs.a: Yes. OCR and the extraction models handle Devanagari and other major Indian scripts on documents such as voter IDs and state-issued certificates. Names are matched across scripts using transliteration, and uncertain matches go to an officer.
No. Aadhaar is masked at intake so only the last four digits remain, and our pipeline does not keep the unmasked image. Any full Aadhaar handling stays within your existing UIDAI-compliant processes.

It can check documents shown or uploaded during a V-CIP session and compare the photograph with the captured image, as an aid to the bank official. The official's live judgement and your V-CIP procedure remain unchanged.

A pilot runs on file exports and needs no core banking change. For production, most banks use a staging table or middleware API, and the timeline depends on your change-management process more than on the models.
